# MM-P1-L4-HP02-S2 Fastener inspection and torque - Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Scope
This procedure defines the required inspection, cleaning, lubrication, and torque verification for structural and pressure boundary fasteners on EQ-P1-L4-HP02. It applies to bolted connections on the press frame, platen assemblies, cylinder mounts, guide columns, and accessory attachments that participate in load transfer or sealing. The intent is to prevent loosening under dynamic load, ensure consistent clamp load, and protect threaded assemblies from corrosion and galling. Related documents: ECN-2026-047, SB-1012, SOP-P1-L4-03.

Background and rationale
Fastener integrity on a hydraulic forging press directly affects safety, dimensional accuracy of forgings, and hydraulic component life. Vibration, thermal cycling from process transfers, and lubricant degradation contribute to preload loss and thread damage. Periodic inspection and controlled re-torque restore clamp load and reveal damaged components early. The hydraulic oil change interval for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 2680 hours; coordinating fastener inspections with the oil change reduces downtime and ensures access during planned maintenance windows. Use of the specified lubricant minimizes compatibility issues; the lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195.

Tools
- Calibrated, traceable torque tool capable of documenting applied torque and capture of tool output in maintenance record. Verify calibration traceability per SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Torque angle measurement accessory if required by fastener type, per manufacturer instruction referenced in ECN-2026-047.
- Clean lint-free rags and solvent compatible with painted and plated surfaces as identified in SB-1012.
- Wire brush and thread chase for light thread cleaning; use only as required and avoid damage to preload surfaces.
- Lubricant CFW-LUB-195 and application equipment (brush or aerosol delivery specified by manufacturer).
- Personal protective equipment per plant requirements in SOP-P1-L4-03.

Procedure
Preparation
- Lock out and tag out energy sources per plant LOTO practices in SOP-P1-L4-03 and render the press mechanically safe for access to bolted connections.
- Identify target fasteners using the equipment assembly drawings and ECN-2026-047. Prioritize fasteners associated with load paths, sealing faces, and cylinder mounts.

Inspection
- Visually inspect each fastener and surrounding area for evidence of corrosion, fretting, paint loss, thread deformation, and witness marks indicating rotation. Document location and condition in the maintenance record.
- For fasteners showing evidence of damage or suspected loss of preload, perform a sleeve or nut removal and thread inspection. Use thread chase only to remove light contamination; replace fasteners that show thread flattening, galling, or significant corrosion.
- Where witness marks are present, compare to previous records to determine whether rotation occurred since the last inspection. Note any discrepancies.

Cleaning and preparation
- Clean bearing surfaces, washer faces, and mating threads with a solvent approved in SB-1012. Remove loose rust and debris. Do not use abrasives that will alter bearing face geometry or seating surfaces.
- Lightly apply lubricant CFW-LUB-195 to threads where manufacturer assembly practice or ECN-2026-047 specifies lubricated torque. Do not apply lubricant to preload bearing faces unless specified by the fastener manufacturer or change control.

Torque application and verification
- Establish the required torque or assembly method from the fastener specification retained with the press assembly drawings in ECN-2026-047. When a torque-plus-angle method is called out use the torque tool with angle capture as required.
- Seat fasteners uniformly where multiple fasteners share a flange or clamp. Apply torque in a cross or star pattern appropriate to the joint geometry until final assembly condition is reached for all fasteners in the joint.
- Use the calibrated torque tool to apply torque and record the tool output to the maintenance record. For critical connections, perform a second pass to verify torque values after the joint has relaxed and re-seated.
- If any fastener fails to achieve the specified torque due to thread stripping or failure of the substrate, do not reuse the fastener. Document the failure and obtain replacement parts and disposition per ECN-2026-047.

Examples and decision logic
- Example: For a collapsed nut or rounded hex head discovered during inspection, remove the fastener and record the failure mode. Replace with new hardware and torque per the specification in ECN-2026-047. Retain removed hardware with the maintenance record until disposition is completed.
- Example: If preload loss is inferred from witness mark displacement but fastener and threads are otherwise acceptable, re-torque to specified assembly values and re-mark with witness paint at the final torque state. Enter the action and justification into the maintenance log.

Records to keep
- Complete an inspection log for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 that includes fastener location identifiers, condition notes, actions taken, lubricant applied (CFW-LUB-195), and torque tool outputs. Attach supporting photos for any degraded or failed hardware.
- Retain calibration certificates for torque tools used, consistent with SOP-P1-L4-03.
- Record linkage to the hydraulic oil change cycle; note that the hydraulic oil change interval for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is 2680 hours as a point of coordination for scheduling.
- File all records in the document control system and reference ECN-2026-047 for parts and replaced hardware disposition.

Acceptance criteria
- All inspected fasteners must meet one of the following conditions: acceptable as-is with no intervention required and documented; acceptable after cleaning and re-torque per referenced specification; or replaced and documented with root cause for replacement.
- Torque verification records must show applied torque values consistent with the fastener specification in ECN-2026-047 and must be supported by calibrated tool output records in the maintenance file.
- Lubricant application must be documented as CFW-LUB-195 where lubrication is specified.
- Any instance of stripped threads, failed fastener, or substrate failure must be documented and reported following ECN-2026-047 and SB-1012 for corrective action and part disposition.

References
- ECN-2026-047
- SB-1012
- SOP-P1-L4-03
